clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A client performing home peritoneal dialysis asks how often the healed catheter exit site should be cleansed. Which teaching is most accurate?

options.A: Cleanse the exit site at least twice weekly and again after each shower or episode of vigorous exercise.
options.B: Stop routine cleansing after the exit site heals and resume care if drainage or marked redness develops.
options.C: Cleanse the exit site about monthly because more frequent routine cleansing increases catheter infection risk.
options.D: Use regular soaking in bath water as the preferred substitute for the prescribed exit-site cleansing routine.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2023 International Society for Peritoneal Dialysis catheter-related infection guideline recommends cleansing the PD catheter exit site at least twice weekly and every time after a shower or vigorous exercise, including running, cycling, swimming, and water sports. It also recommends continuing exit-site care for as long as the catheter remains in place, even if PD is interrupted or discontinued. The guideline notes that less-frequent care has been associated with higher odds of catheter-related infection and emphasizes keeping the exit site clean and dry after water exposure or vigorous exercise. Therefore option A accurately states the current routine cleansing frequency.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach current routine peritoneal-dialysis exit-site cleansing frequency: at least twice weekly and after showers or vigorous exercise while the catheter remains in place.
semantic_correction.source_locator: Exit site care — recommend cleansing the exit site at least twice weekly and every time after a shower or vigorous exercise, including running, cycling, swimming, and water sports (1C); continue PD catheter exit-site care for as long as the catheter remains in place; supporting text notes care less often than twice weekly was associated with higher odds of catheter-related infection
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Current ISPD guidance recommends routine PD catheter exit-site cleansing at least twice weekly and after each shower or vigorous exercise, with ongoing exit-site care while the catheter remains in place.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only' distractor cue, shortened the correct answer, and anchored the item to the exact ISPD 2023 routine cleansing frequency without conflating routine care with treatment of an infected exit site.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — invasive-device infection prevention
audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest and one distractor used absolute wording. The revised item directly tests current routine PD exit-site cleansing frequency with parallel alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches the ISPD recommendation for at least twice-weekly cleansing plus cleansing after showers or vigorous exercise.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Routine exit-site care continues while the catheter remains in place rather than stopping after healing.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Monthly cleansing is less frequent than the ISPD recommendation and is not supported as safer.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Routine water soaking does not replace the prescribed exit-site cleansing protocol and can increase water exposure.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone reproduces the current ISPD routine cleansing schedule without confusing routine care with infected-site management.
cueing_check: All four choices are routine exit-site care schedules or methods of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.

checks: ongoing care while catheter remains in place verified directly
routine care distinguished from daily care suggested for an infected exit site
no unsupported universal cleansing agent introduced
